partners.mechanism_chain: CYP7B1 (HGNC:2575) —DISRUPTS→ cholesterol biosynthesis and transport (REACT:R-HSA-116883); CYP7B1 (HGNC:2575) —DECREASES→ steroid hormones (CHEBI:24611); cholesterol biosynthesis and transport (REACT:R-HSA-116883) —LEADS_TO→ spastic paraplegia (HP:0001256); steroid hormones (CHEBI:24611) —LEADS_TO→ spastic paraplegia (HP:0001256); POMC (HGNC:9195) —DISRUPTS→ hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis regulation (REACT:R-HSA-168760); POMC (HGNC:9195) —DECREASES→ melanocortin peptides (CHEBI:50834); hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis regulation (REACT:R-HSA-168760) —LEADS_TO→ obesity (HP:0005101); melanocortin peptides (CHEBI:50834) —LEADS_TO→ obesity (HP:0005101); steroid hormones (CHEBI:24611) —DISRUPTS→ hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis regulation (REACT:R-HSA-168760). Loss-of-function mutations in CYP7B1 disrupt cholesterol biosynthesis and transport, leading to altered steroid hormone levels which can affect neuronal function and contribute to spastic paraplegia. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in POMC disrupt the production of melanocortin peptides, impacting the HPA axis and leading to obesity. We hypothesize that dysregulation of steroid hormones due to CYP7B1 deficiency can impinge on the HPA axis, creating a shared mechanistic convergence point with POMC deficiency and contributing to overlapping neuroendocrine and metabolic dysregulation.
